description:
`me` lets an app you authorize read the parts of your UnitySVC profile you choose, and, only if you also allow it, update them.

The gateway answers `me` itself (`me://user`): there is no upstream. Today `me` serves one resource, your `profile`; others may be added beside it. A read returns everything the calling key's `service:me` grant allows that you have set, served from your account's routing context: the profile paths the grant's `profile` option lists (a section such as `research`, or one value inside it such as `address.state`). A value you never set and one you did not share are both simply absent, so an app learns only what it may read. Whether a section is public plays no part, and no request parameter can change what a key reads. A write is forwarded to UnitySVC, which checks the grant and that the key's owner may edit the account, then merges the data into the section. `me` exports two permissions and nothing else: `read` and `write`. `invoke`, and the `service:*` and `*` wildcards that stand for it, never reach `me`. A grant's `profile` option defaults to nothing, so it must list what it covers; `profile=*` (the whole profile) is for keys you create yourself, never for a key issued to another service. `me` is not billed.

Call `GET /me` (the same as `GET /me/profile`) for everything your key may read, or `GET /me/profile/<path>` for one path, with a UnitySVC key whose policy grants `service:me` with `read`, e.g. `{"object": "service:me", "permissions": ["read"], "options": "profile=research,address.state"}`; the answer is `{"profile": {...}}`. To update a section, `POST /me` with `{"name": "<section>", "public": <bool>, "data": {...}}` using a key whose grant also holds `write` and lists that whole section. Edit your profile itself under **Profile** in the dashboard.

profile.description: Profile paths this grant covers (the profile resource's option; each me resource has one named after it): a section name (research), or a section followed by keys of its object data (address.state). A read returns these paths where they are set. A write needs the whole section listed. * is the whole profile, for keys you create yourself only. Unset covers nothing.

name: me

payout_price.description: Not billed: reading and updating your own profile is free

summary: Let an app read the parts of your UnitySVC profile you choose through `/me`, and update them only if you also allow it.
